author: WP17
summary: Short chapter framing free-direct and free-api as narrow sibling libraries beneath the 2D-only FREEDIRECT renderer: the dependency chain, 2D scope, pinning, why the layer distinction matters and a status matrix. Mostly current; corrected where stub methods report success, where free-direct is called pinned (nothing pins it) and by the missing CNA CI lane. The site had only ecosystem-level summaries; the new deep dive adds the chain, status-tag census, fopen containment and inherited limits.

concepts.text: free-direct is a separately versioned compatibility library for a deliberately narrow, game-driven DirectDraw/DirectSound/DirectPlay-shaped surface, and free-api supplies selected Win32-shaped types and helpers beneath it; neither is the CNA framework and neither aims to emulate every Windows API.

concepts.text: CNA's FREEDIRECT renderer adapts SpriteBatch, textures and render targets to free-direct's DirectDraw-shaped objects, using DirectDraw only and CNA's own SDL_Window passed as the HWND.

concepts.text: free-direct uses SDL3 internally, but that does not make FREEDIRECT part of the SDL_RENDERER family: it never calls SDL's 2D texture API, only DirectDraw-shaped COM calls.

concepts.text: Ownership and errors cross explicit boundaries in the chain GraphicsDevice/SpriteBatch -> FreeDirect adapter -> free-direct surfaces and presentation -> free-api host helpers; free-direct adds ../free-api itself when no free-api target exists and links it PUBLIC, while the free-eggbert and planetblupi games add free-api explicitly first.

concepts.text: Unsupported COM methods do not uniformly fail: QueryInterface stubs return DDERR_UNSUPPORTED, but IDirectDrawSurface::IsLost() always returns DD_OK and Restore() always succeeds, so surface loss is unobservable.
